SFM.long: The author holds a long position in the security mentioned.
SFM.c1: Store expansion is the growth driver. The cited 2025 annual report planned 40 more stores in 2026, and five-year revenue growth is given as 6.36%.
SFM.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. The stated P/FCF of 17.1 is the current multiple, so this score is 0.
SFM.c4: The moat section ties the organic and animal-welfare brand to higher gross margins than traditional grocers, and names inflation as the threat. That is a narrow intangibles claim.
SFM.c5: No named operating result for the people running Sprouts. Buybacks are mentioned without a price or a person.
SFM.c6: The article says the current multiple is reasonable and the position is for stability. It does not say the market is wrong.
SFM.c7: Forty store openings during 2026 are named, without a specific date. Later comparable-sales checks are not a dated re-rating event.
flags: H1 2026 comparable store sales were -1.4%.
Inflation could push customers to cheaper chains.
SBC is 9.07% of free cash flow.
No price target.

BPC.CN.long: I own shares of The Precision Peptide Company (CSE: BPC / OTCQB: PNGAF), bought in the open market.
BPC.CN.c1: Needle-free access to peptides is the growth driver. Management describes four channels, three of them already live, in a category where injections have been the barrier.
BPC.CN.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. The move from about 45 cents to about 30 cents is a price history, not a target.
BPC.CN.c4: Vertical integration and public reporting are described. They are not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
BPC.CN.c5: Paul Katz is named as the former CEO of Ving, which exited in 2022, with no sale figure. That is a partial prior result.
BPC.CN.c6: The shares fell from about 45 cents to about 30 cents while a warrant block was outstanding, and the article says that block has now been exercised, so the overhang should not still be in the price.
BPC.CN.c7: The Thymosin Alpha 1 patch and channel growth are named over the next six months, with no calendar date.
flags: US peptide rules are changing and are outside the company control.
No price target and no cash-runway figure.
The warrant overhang the article cites has already been exercised.

BADEF.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of BADEF either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
BADEF.c1: Copper demand for grids, vehicles, and data centers is the growth driver. Leviathan is the named discovery, with a second target at Hook and two more zones planned.
BADEF.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. The rating change from strong buy to buy is not a price.
BADEF.c3: Insiders continued to steadily purchase shares on the open market in the months preceding the management addition. No CEO percentage is stated. The new team's C$4.5 million was a private placement, and Barrick's 10% is not the CEO's stake.
BADEF.c4: Road access, power lines, and a US location are described. They are not argued as one of the five moat types.
BADEF.c5: George Ogilvie's Arizona Sonoran team advanced Cactus from about C$125 million in July 2021 to a Hudbay acquisition at about C$2.0 billion in 2026, a 16-fold gain. That is one result with figures.
BADEF.c6: The article says the recent drill results were somewhat ignored. It does not say why that discount should close, and it says the chart does not look favorable.
BADEF.c7: The drill program is to expand beyond two rigs in 2027, with Southern Flats and Pegasus named. No calendar date.
flags: Cash of C$25.6 million against C$18.8 million of burn over four quarters, with a raise described as likely in 2027.
The author cut the rating from strong buy to buy because the chart does not look favorable.
No price target.
Explorer risk, including dilution, is stated as the main risk.

BLND.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
BLND.c1: Autopilot, released commercially on July 2, 2026, and a mortgage-volume recovery are the growth drivers. The CEO said the AI path already supports 10% to 15% incremental growth in 2027.
BLND.c2: The base case is more than 2.5x in two to three years, which the article states as a 37% to 60% IRR. The midpoint is about 48% a year.
BLND.c3: The article says the CEO owns 31% of the voting power today, and 82% if every equity award were exercised.
BLND.c4: The installed mortgage workflow is the switching cost. A Fiserv leader says changing vendors after an integration is a lot of effort, and names the threat that a larger firm could build its own system.
BLND.c5: Cash operating expense in Q1 2026 was 72% below the Q4 2021 peak, and the company is cash-flow positive after selling Title365. That is one operating result with figures.
BLND.c6: The stock is flat with the March 3 Autopilot launch, so the price assigns nothing to the agent, and the article says a Haveli bid or Q3 results are what would put that value in the price.
BLND.c7: Autopilot is not in the numbers until the Q3 financials, and that release is tied to whether the agent is showing up.
flags: 56% of recent revenue is the mortgage suite, which moves with rates.
Top five customers were 39% of 2025 revenue.
Autopilot adoption could be slower than hoped.

SMWB.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
SMWB.c1: AI data licenses are the growth driver. One $47 million deal, about $8 million a year for three years, adds about 500 basis points of growth on a $290 million base.
SMWB.c2: At $400 million of revenue and a 30% free-cash-flow margin, a 10% yield is $14.50 a share, about 109% above the price, in about three years. That is about 29% a year.
SMWB.c3: Founder and CEO Or Offer bought about $300,000 of stock this year. Three other directors bought about $1 million in aggregate.
SMWB.c4: Ten-plus years of first-party web, app, and retail data across 190 countries is the intangible. The threat is that LLM search replaces SEO, and the article argues customers will need both tools.
SMWB.c5: Operating margin went from -33% to 7% in Q3 2024 while revenue grew 18%. The later AI sales push then missed the deals it was built for, so the record is one result with figures.
SMWB.c6: The market is pricing SEO as a casualty of LLMs. The article says the $47 million deal is not yet in sell-side estimates, so those numbers have to come up as the contract shows through.
SMWB.c7: Or Offer said he intends to retire within 12 months, and the article ties that window to a possible sale of the data asset.
flags: The founder plans to retire within 12 months.
AI data contracts could be one-time if they do not renew.
Dilution is still about 3% a year.

SRTA.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
SRTA.c1: US transplants and normothermic regional perfusion are the growth driver. Deceased-donor transplants set a record for twelve straight years, and the community is targeting 50,000 transplants in 2026.
SRTA.c2: The base case is about $9.85 a share on FY2029 EBITDA at 12x, held 2.5 years from $5.23. That is a 29% IRR, inside 25% to 40%.
SRTA.c4: The moat section names a national logistics network, scarce perfusion staff that hospitals rent rather than employ, and one accountable provider across recovery and flight. TransMedics is the named threat, limited to organs on its own device.
SRTA.c5: Will Heyburn and Melissa Tomkiel sold the passenger business to Joby for up to $125 million and bought HLT-NRP at a mid-single-digit EBITDA multiple. That is one capital-allocation result with figures.
SRTA.c6: The shares still carry the old Blade air-taxi identity and a GAAP loss. The article says each 2026 quarter of Keystone revenue is what makes the two-segment healthcare business show up in a screen.
SRTA.c7: Each 2026 quarter is tied to the thesis, because that is when a full period of the clinical business lands next to organic logistics growth.
flags: The clinical business is barely a year old.
GAAP losses and FY2025 cash outflow.
Customer base is concentrated in 55 organ-procurement organizations.

RDEIY.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
RDEIY.c1: The government-approved 2026-2031 plan is the growth driver. It lifts average annual capex by more than half and the regulated asset base at about a 9% annual rate, after a flat decade.
RDEIY.c2: The author expects a low-double-digit compound return for five years, and about €25 a share in 2031, more than 60% above the then price before dividends. That price gain is about 10% a year.
RDEIY.c3: The CEO's annual bonus can reach 110% of a €350,000 base and is tied to the capex plan, profit before tax, and return on invested capital. No ownership percentage is stated.
RDEIY.c4: Redeia is the only high-voltage operator in Spain by government decree, with no end date. The article argues the physics of transmission and names the blackout liability and the 2032 rate reset as the threats.
RDEIY.c5: On the CEO's watch the fiber business sold 49% to KKR in 2021 at 22.1x EBITDA, €2.3 billion. That is one capital-allocation result with figures.
RDEIY.c6: The shares fell €4, or €2.2 billion, after the April 2025 blackout while other European grid operators rose. The March 2026 ENTSO report is what the article says should take the blame off Redeia.
RDEIY.c7: The CNMC investigation, with a maximum penalty of €60 million, is named and has no decision date.
flags: A blackout liability is unprovisioned.
Free cash flow is negative while the new assets are built.
The 2032-2037 allowed return depends on Spanish bond yields.

STC.TO.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
STC.TO.c1: The infrastructure segment is the growth driver. Management said voice grew 19% and MSP and data grew 9%, and AI agents need that kind of communications infrastructure.
STC.TO.c2: The author says the business is worth about $11 a share, against a publish close of $5.75. Over the default two years that is 38% a year.
STC.TO.c3: Chairman Norm Worthington owns just under 20%. He is not the CEO and not a founder of Sangoma.
STC.TO.c4: The applications market is described as commoditized. Low churn is stated, and it is not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism and a threat.
STC.TO.c5: The team that joined in fall 2023 has recurring revenue at about 92% and monthly churn at 0.79%. The same team missed a 10% organic-growth hope and reported 3% to 4% declines, so the record is partial.
STC.TO.c6: The shares are priced as a UCaaS company that missed growth targets. The article says the overlooked infrastructure segment and the chair's wish for liquidity are why a sale process can close the gap.
STC.TO.c7: An investment bank was retained about two months before the write-up to review a sale. No end date is given.
flags: The strategic review can fail.
Applications revenue has been declining about 6% to 7%.
Infrastructure growth could slow.

ADCT.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
ADCT.c1: Label expansion of ZYNLONTA is the growth driver. The existing third-line franchise is about $74 million of revenue, and the article expects new uses to multiply that.
ADCT.c2: If LOTIS-5 adds nothing, the author still sees more than $300 million of revenue and more than $150 million of EBIT, worth about $5 a share. From the $1.26 close over two years that is about 99% a year.
ADCT.c4: An approved drug franchise is described. It is not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
ADCT.c5: No named operating result for the people running the company. The trial figures belong to the drug, not to a person's record.
ADCT.c6: The stock fell about 70% because LOTIS-5 was worse than expected, and the article says the market is pricing a real chance the drug is pulled. The commercial case is that third-line use stays and LOTIS-7 is the actual driver.
ADCT.c7: LOTIS-7, which has finished enrolling 100 patients, reads out top-line data in the fourth quarter.
flags: LOTIS-5 showed no overall-survival benefit and a death imbalance in older European patients.
The FDA can reject the second-line expansion.
The $5 value assumes LOTIS-7 and the marginal-zone use both arrive.

FMBL.company: Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach
FMBL.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
FMBL.c1: The Fidelity securities-based loan program is the growth driver. The author uses $1.5 billion of loans in three to four years, about $90 million of extra interest income, against $430 million of 2025 interest income.
FMBL.c2: The author says a low-teens IRR over the next five years is reasonable. That is below 25% a year. No dollar target is stated.
FMBL.c4: A 1.5% cost of funds and about $3 billion of non-interest-bearing deposits are the cost advantage. No threat to that deposit franchise is named, so the moat stays narrow.
FMBL.c5: New hires are described as experienced and were introduced at the annual meeting. No result with figures is attached to them.
FMBL.c6: The partnership is not officially disclosed, and the stock is at 78% of tangible book against a 172% average for banks with $10 billion to $50 billion of assets. The loan ramp is what the article says will show up in earnings.
FMBL.c7: A proxy item would cut the merger vote from 80% to 60%, and a $40 million repurchase is being sought. Neither has a date.
flags: The Fidelity investment is inferred, not confirmed by the company.
A sale is explicitly not the thesis.
Controlling holders have not pursued steps to make the shares more liquid.

G.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
G.c1: Deploying AI inside workflows Genpact already runs is the growth driver. Advanced Technology Solutions, 27% of revenue, grew 24.3% in the first quarter of 2026, and the core segment still grew 1.4%.
G.c2: With 3% long-term growth, normalized earnings of $3.87 are worth $48.40. From the $30.48 close over two years that is 26% a year.
G.c4: Workflow knowledge is the switching cost, and spreading the fixed cost of an AI system across many clients is the cost advantage. The threat is that a client uses Genpact to document a process and then takes it in-house.
G.c5: No named operating result for the people running Genpact. The GE spinoff is company history.
G.c6: A reverse DCF says the price implies zero or negative perpetual growth, because the market treats task automation as losing the client. Eight quarters of growth, including the core segment, are what the article says contradicts that.
flags: The core segment could shrink before the technology segment replaces it.
A client could insource a process after Genpact documents it.
No dated catalyst.

AW.TO.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
AW.TO.c1: Store growth and the Canadian Pret A Manger rights are the growth drivers. System sales have compounded at 6% for 20 years, and 2026 targets include 2% unit growth.
AW.TO.c2: The author says the base case should return 11% to 12%, from a dividend yield above 5% and earnings growth of 6% to 7%. That is below 25% a year.
AW.TO.c3: Insiders, including two former CEOs, and TorQuest own 58%. That is an aggregate holding. The current CEO's own stake is not stated.
AW.TO.c4: The brand is described as domestic and strong, and 70% of new stores are opened by existing franchisees. No threat to that position is named, so the moat stays narrow.
AW.TO.c5: The CEO has been at the company for more than 30 years and in the job for nine, after running marketing and operations. No result is tied to those years with figures.
AW.TO.c6: The article calls the price reasonable and the return ordinary, with extra upside if the company is sold. It does not say the market is wrong.
AW.TO.c7: Three or four Pret stores are planned for 2026, with no opening date. A sale is described as a few years away.
flags: Same-store sales targets are well below the long-run pace.
The head-lease structure is a large liability if franchisees fail.
A sale is a hope, not a process.

FULC.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
FULC.c1: This is a cash shell. The last drug, pociredir, was discontinued, and the value is the cash plus a reverse merger. That is an asset value, not a growth runway.
FULC.c2: Net cash is about $4.44 a share against a $3.62 close. Over the default two years that is about 11% a year. The author says the deal should be near term and does not give a year count.
FULC.c4: A failed program and a cash balance are not one of the five moat types.
FULC.c5: Tang Capital is named as a buyer of shells, with a list of completed deals and no return figure on those deals. That is a partial record for a holder, not for the remaining management.
FULC.c6: The stock is below net cash because the drug failed. The article says Leerink's process and holders of more than 40% of the shares are what force a fair deal, as in the BOLD, NextCure, and VYNE mergers.
FULC.c7: A transaction is expected in the near term. No date is set. The June announcements are already past.
flags: The reverse merger can be dilutive, as the cited shells retained about 1% to 4%.
Lease and severance cash can come in above the estimate.
No date is set for a deal.

ACRE.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
ACRE.c1: The pitch is a cheap book and two troubled loans, not a growth franchise. Loan demand is described as inflecting, and that is a cycle, so this scores as an asset value.
ACRE.c2: A 10% yield on the $0.15 quarterly dividend is a $6 stock. From the $4.52 close over two years that is 15% a year.
ACRE.c4: An external mortgage REIT priced below book is not one of the five moat types.
ACRE.c5: The current CEO, Bryan Donohoe, is described as having a credit background and as not yet having turned the book around. Ares's record on this vehicle is the halving of book value.
ACRE.c6: A 13% yield prices a dividend cut. The article says resolving the Chicago office loan and the Brooklyn condo loan, then relending the proceeds, is what makes the $0.15 dividend covered.
ACRE.c7: Construction on the Brooklyn project runs through fall 2026, and the article ties that finish to a takeout of the loan. A sale process on the Chicago building is described as active.
flags: The two largest loans are not accruing.
Further credit migration would delay the recovery.
Ares can keep neglecting the vehicle.

FINV.long: I and/or others I advise hold a material investment in the issuer's securities.
FINV.c1: The international book is the growth driver. It was 30% of revenue and 8% of adjusted operating profit in the first quarter of 2026.
FINV.c2: The author says 50% to 100% upside over three to five years. The midpoint, 75% over four years, is 15% a year.
FINV.c4: Scale, technology, and cheaper customer acquisition are named in one sentence. They are not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
FINV.c5: The company is called best in class and a pioneer. No named person's result is given with figures.
FINV.c6: The low multiple is blamed on the old peer-to-peer history and the 2025 rate cap. A recovery in sentiment is the hoped-for close, and no mechanism is given for why the gap has to shut.
FINV.c7: No future event is named. Dividends and buybacks are described as ongoing.
flags: Further rate caps in China or in Indonesia and the Philippines.
A credit downturn hits the first-loss exposure.
No dated catalyst.

ESI.TO.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of ESVIF; PTEN either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
ESI.TO.c1: The U.S. drilling recovery, scarce high-spec rigs, and international activity are the growth driver. The Citadel deal adds six high-spec rigs for US$65 million, mostly for Occidental.
ESI.TO.c2: The author says Ensign trades at 0.5x book and should trade at least at book value during the upcycle. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 41% a year.
ESI.TO.c4: High-spec scarcity and maintenance-only capex are described. They are not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
ESI.TO.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The Citadel purchase is a transaction, not a track record.
ESI.TO.c6: The shares sold off with the May oil top as if this were a normal supply-flood cycle. The correction is higher dayrates, because contractors are keeping capex to maintenance.
ESI.TO.c7: Higher dayrates over the next few quarters, and possible 2027 capex plans if oil stays high for two or three months, are named and undated.
flags: Kuwait and Bahrain rigs are suspended while the five Oman rigs stay active.
The Citadel deal pushed out the debt-reduction goal.
The street average target is only about 10% upside and is not the endpoint used.

FIGR.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of FIGR either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
FIGR.c1: The lending marketplace, Figure Connect, and the Kiavi deal are the growth drivers. Q2 sales were $225.6 million, up 95% from Q2 2025, and the author forecasts $950 million in 2026 and $1.23 billion in 2027.
FIGR.c2: The stated target is $44.80, from 15x 2027 EBITDA of $642 million plus net corporate cash. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 25% a year.
FIGR.c4: The distribution network is the network effect. Figure Connect was about 65% of activity, up from 42% in Q2 2025, with 102 active partners and 489 in total, up 26% sequentially. The threats named are lower Connect take rates, U.S. housing and rates, the Kiavi integration, and regulation.
FIGR.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The Kiavi deal, $717 million in cash with Sixth Street, is a transaction.
FIGR.c6: The shares fell into a $25 to $35 range and the author says $28 is reasonable against a $44.80 value. The reason that gap has to close is not specific.
FIGR.c7: Kiavi volume will be reflected in Q4 results, a named quarter inside 24 months and tied to the growth thesis. The Q3 preliminary figures were already released on October 6.
flags: Stock-based compensation was $52 million in the first half.
Connect take rates are lower, so sales can lag volume.
The business is sensitive to U.S. housing and interest rates.
Kiavi integration and regulatory uncertainty.

ONDS.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of ONDS, PLTR either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
ONDS.c1: A defense-prime buildout is the growth driver. The full-year target is $525 million to $550 million of 2026 revenue, with a $1 billion exit run rate.
ONDS.c2: The bull case is the one the author adopts: $20.87 at the end of 2027, from $1.3 billion of revenue at 10x sales. The horizon is the end of 2027, about 1.22 years. That is about 155% a year.
ONDS.c4: Prime-contractor status is efficient scale: Ondas owns the customer vehicle after the Mistral merger, including the $982 million Army IDIQ. The budget trend is the FY2027 request, and the threats named are dilution and the execution ramp.
ONDS.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. Insider sales of about $44 million, with no open-market purchases, are not an operating record.
ONDS.c6: The market is pricing the share count, which rose from 93 million to about 590 million, rather than the cash and the backlog. The correction is revenue catching that share count.
ONDS.c7: Adjusted EBITDA profitability at the operating platform in Q4 2026 is a named quarter inside 24 months and is tied to the thesis.
flags: Share count rose from 93 million to about 590 million, with 45 million more DZYNE shares due on January 4, 2027.
One customer was 40% of Q2 revenue, and $187 million of backlog sits in the Middle East.
More than 20 companies were acquired in 14 months.
Insiders sold about $44 million with no open-market purchases.

OUST.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of OUST either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
OUST.c1: Physical-AI perception is the growth driver. REV8 and the StereoLabs deal move Ouster from a LiDAR supplier to a camera, compute, and software package, and management's stated growth range is 30% to 50% a year.
OUST.c2: The stated target is $88.27 in 2028, from 15x sales on $452.54 million of revenue and about 76.90 million shares. The author says the horizon is about 18 months. That is about 78% a year.
OUST.c4: The one-stop perception package is a narrow switching cost: customers take cameras, LiDAR, compute, and software from one vendor, and REV8 is backward compatible with REV7 housings. Orders are described as coming in faster than expected. The threat is that growth which only meets guidance has been punished before.
OUST.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The author's own prior Ouster article is not a record of the people running the company.
OUST.c6: The article says the market priced the stock on macroeconomics and on the old consumer-ADAS path. The reason that view has to change is left as a return of last summer's enthusiasm.
OUST.c7: REV8 sales are said to ramp from Q4 2026 through 2028, a named quarter inside 24 months and tied to the growth thesis.
flags: The 2027 profitability comment comes from an interview, not official guidance.
The stock has been punished when revenue only met the forecast.
Further equity awards can lift the 76.90 million share count used in the target.

PRPO.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of PRPO either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
PRPO.c1: On-site cancer testing is the growth driver. The product is a kit-and-instrument model, and 2025 revenue grew 30% to $24.0 million.
PRPO.c2: The stated endpoint is the probability-weighted 2031 price of $160, not the $45 to $52 figure, which is that $160 discounted back to today. The horizon is the end of 2031, about 5.22 years. That is about 46% a year.
PRPO.c3: Ilan Danieli owns about 2,850 shares outright. Against the stated share count that holding is under 1%, so the CEO's own stake is 0. Officers and directors hold 16.6%, an aggregate of at least 10%, so the score is 0.25.
PRPO.c4: The kit placed in the customer's lab is a narrow switching cost. The article says turnaround and pathologist training create switching costs once the instrument is installed, and the threat is slow conversion of new labs.
PRPO.c5: Ilan Danieli founded Precipio Diagnostics in 2011 and still runs it. No separate sale or turnaround figure is given for that record.
PRPO.c6: The shares still trade at roughly the revenue multiple of the cash-burn years. The correction is proof that new-lab sales and cash flow are showing up.
PRPO.c7: November 2026 results are tied to pipeline conversion and cash flow, and the March 2027 10-K is tied to whether the substantial-doubt language comes off.
flags: The filings still include a going-concern statement.
One customer was 26% of 2025 revenue.
The commercial build depends on distributors and a sales team rehired in January 2026.
A data-security class action is at an early stage, with no liability recorded.

SIRI.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of SIRI either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
SIRI.c1: The case is a cheap spectrum-and-cash-flow asset with buybacks. YouTube and the 360L rollout are named, but they are not the re-rating the author adopts.
SIRI.c2: The scenario the author calls the bear case is a share price of about $40 in five years. That is about 8% a year, so this score is 0.
SIRI.c4: Low churn and the 360L platform are a narrow switching cost: the subscription can attach to the person rather than the car, and 360L is already half of new trials with a path to 90% by 2030. The threat is a subscriber spiral if carmakers drop the receivers.
SIRI.c5: No named Sirius XM operating result is given for the people running it. The DaVita buyback history is another company.
SIRI.c6: The market is pricing the equity as if the radio business were already dead, with enterprise value near the spectrum value. The correction is buybacks restarting in 2027, while 360L and the YouTube deal show the deterioration has not arrived.
SIRI.c7: Large-scale buybacks are said to restart in 2027, a named year inside 24 months and tied to the re-rating.
flags: Self-pay subscribers are slightly down from Q2 2024.
Net debt is stated at $9.5 billion.
The iHeart combination is described as aborted for now.
The five-year bear case is under 25% a year from the publish close.

YLLXF.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of YLLXF, SRUUF either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
YLLXF.c1: The case is a passive holding of uranium at a discount to net asset value. Demand growth for nuclear power is the commodity backdrop, not a company growth driver.
YLLXF.c2: The author says the shares have the potential to double this cycle. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. A double in two years is about 41% a year.
YLLXF.c4: Owning uranium in storage is not one of the five moat types.
YLLXF.c5: No named person's operating result at Yellow Cake is given with figures. The author's own seven-year portfolio return is not the company's record.
YLLXF.c6: Uranium equities are down on weak sentiment while the spot price is up about 10%, and the discount to net asset value is 20% to 25% against a usual 5% to 15%. The article says that discount is unlikely to last forever, without a mechanism.
YLLXF.c7: A move in the uranium price toward $130 to $150 a pound this cycle is named and undated.
flags: A deflationary move could cut the uranium spot price and widen the discount.
The primary listing is in London. The scored line is the U.S. ticker YLLXF.
The double is stated as potential this cycle, with no date.

VIOT.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of VIOT either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
VIOT.c1: A return to growth in home water systems is the driver, after national subsidies for purifiers ended. The article cites an 8.7% market growth rate and sales outside China.

The dividend can be changed.

BLSH.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of BLSH, COIN, BTC-USD either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.

BLSH.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures.

BLSH.c7: Tokenization and the Equiniti deal are named and undated.

The business is tied to the bitcoin price.
Regulation, a platform breach, or slower tokenization are the risks the article names.

CHWY.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of CHWY either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.

CHWY.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The margin path from 3% to 5.7% is stated as the company's, not a person's.
CHWY.c6: The market is pricing Chewy as a struggling pet retailer after the June guidance cut. The correction is that Autoship customers stay, and the margin path is still intact when the pet market recovers.
CHWY.c7: Ending FY 2026 with 60 vet clinics, and about $50 million of annualized AI savings in FY 2027, are named without a calendar date.
flags: FY 2026 sales guidance was cut in June as pet owners pulled back.
The DCF still needs the operating margin to more than double.
BC Partners owns about 44% and has been selling.
Amazon and Walmart can compete on price and delivery.

CLMT.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of CLMT either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.

A two-to-four-week Shreveport shutdown is planned for November to December.
Today's specialty crack spreads are well above the $25 level the author calls normal.

DSVSF.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of DSVSF, AG, EXK, SVM, PAAS either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
DSVSF.c1: Growing gold production at Porcupine, plus the Cordero silver project, is the driver. Management's chart shows the potential to triple production in five years.
DSVSF.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. The past share-price gain is not a target.
DSVSF.c4: The Timmins location and the new Mexican permits are described. They are not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
DSVSF.c5: Tony Makuch, Chairman, President, and CEO, was named CEO of the year by Kitco. That is an award, with no operating result of his given in figures.
DSVSF.c6: The upgrade rests on gold and silver having further to run and on the company being well managed. The article does not say the market is wrong about this stock.
DSVSF.c7: The CEO said the company is poised for a strong second half. No calendar date is given. Tripling production is a five-year statement.
flags: All-in sustaining costs of $1,950 to $2,250 an ounce are above the industry average cited.
Cordero still has to be built after the October permits.
The author says the shares are thinly traded.
Gold and silver prices are volatile, and the article is an upgrade from hold.

ECO.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of ECO, DHT either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
ECO.c1: The case is a spot-rate spike in crude tankers, not a secular growth driver. The fleet is eight VLCCs and ten Suezmaxes, mostly on the spot market.
ECO.c2: Fair value is $135 a share on a 15% yield against a $20 dividend. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 17% a year.
ECO.c4: A young fleet and Strait of Hormuz voyages are described. They are not argued as one of the five moat types.
ECO.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The stock's gain since the author's earlier articles is not the company's record.
ECO.c6: The market is still using the author's old estimates, while spot VLCCs are argued to be earning about $1 million a day. The correction is the Q4 dividend, which the author puts near 26% of the market cap.
ECO.c7: Q4 earnings and the dividend are a named quarter inside 24 months and are the thesis.
flags: The rate case depends on the Strait of Hormuz staying disrupted.
The author says current rates are not sustainable for many quarters.
The shares trade above NAV, and a secondary offering is named as possible.
One vessel was hit at the CPC terminal.

HIMS.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of HIMS either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
HIMS.c1: The core subscription business is the growth driver. The author uses a 17% revenue growth rate through 2030, and the Novo channel is described as about 100,000 new members a month.
HIMS.c2: The stated fair value is about $41 a share, from a 2030 exit multiple discounted to today. No hold period is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 17% a year.
HIMS.c4: The shift from compounded drugs to branded GLP-1s is described, including the margin drop. It is not argued as one of the five moat types.
HIMS.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The author's family-portfolio return is not the company's record.
HIMS.c6: The market repriced the whole company on a peptide decision the author values at about $3 a share. The correction is the core subscription math, about $38 to $39, plus the Novo adds.
HIMS.c7: Novo's Wegovy wholesale-cost cut on 1 January 2027, and Eli Lilly's planned retatrutide filing in the first quarter of 2027, are named dates inside 24 months and are tied to the thesis.

Gross margin fell from about 76% to about 64%.
The FTC sued the company on 29 July 2026 over subscription cancellation.
The peptide piece is worth about $3 a share in the base case and is not the core target.

GTLB.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of GTLB either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
GTLB.c1: Agentic coding and enterprise demand for sovereignty are the growth drivers. Net ARR grew 42% year over year, and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $1,129 million to $1,133 million.
GTLB.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. Peer scenarios are described without a share price.
GTLB.c4: Self-managed and sovereign deployment is a moderate switching cost for regulated customers. Ultimate is 59% of ARR and grew 35%, and the threat is GitHub restoring reliability and bundling the product.
GTLB.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. Dmitriy Zaporozhets is named as the founder, and the article does not say he still runs it.
GTLB.c6: Reported revenue grew 21% while net ARR grew 42% and first orders doubled. The article says the payoff shows up in 2027, when this year's investment year is behind it.
GTLB.c7: Orbit is set to become generally available next month, and 2027 is the year the article ties to the re-rating. Both are inside 24 months.
flags: GitHub could fix reliability and lean on Microsoft's distribution.
Consumption credits could replace seat revenue.
The shares are up 47% this year and trade at 53x forward earnings.
OpenAI is reported to be building an internal alternative.

MGM.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of MGM either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
MGM.c1: The case is a cheap lease-adjusted cash flow and a buyback, with softer room rates. It is not a secular growth story.
MGM.c2: The base sum of the parts is about $45. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 24% a year.
MGM.c4: The Strip portfolio is efficient scale and an intangible. The resorts sit under the VICI lease, Strip room revenue has weakened, and the threat is rent that does not fall.
MGM.c5: About $9.7 billion of buybacks since the end of 2020 cut the share count by about half, at an average price a little under $40.
MGM.c6: The market is treating a financing failure as a broken business. The correction is that rates, not the resorts, ended the $48.30 bid.
MGM.c7: The October 28 quarterly report is tied to an easy Las Vegas comparison and to whether buybacks resumed.
flags: Strip RevPAR fell in the four reported quarters through June.
Rent is fixed and was $2.26 billion in 2025.
MGM China EBITDAR fell 15% in the quarter.
Osaka does not open until 2030, and the bear case is about $27.

MFIC.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of MFIC, ARCC, FDUS, OBDC, BXSL either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
MFIC.c1: The case is a floating-rate loan book and a discount to net asset value. Higher rates may lift income. It is not a secular growth story.
MFIC.c2: The price-to-NAV range is 0.8x to 0.9x on a $13.37 net asset value, so the midpoint is $11.37. No horizon is stated, so the hold is 2 years. That is about 16% a year.
MFIC.c4: A first-lien loan book is not one of the five moat types.
MFIC.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures.
MFIC.c6: The shares fell to a 37% discount to net asset value while coverage rose to 129% after the dividend cut. The correction is a move toward 0.8x to 0.9x if net asset value stabilizes and non-accruals come down.
MFIC.c7: Further rate increases over the next year, and higher portfolio yields in the quarters ahead, are named without a calendar date.
flags: Non-accruals rose to 2.8% of fair value.
Net asset value has been falling faster than at Ares and Blue Owl.
The dividend was cut 18.4% in the first quarter.

KRKNF.c1: Autonomous underwater vehicles and the Covelya acquisition are the growth driver. Management guides to $290 million to $320 million of 2026 revenue, about triple the prior year.
KRKNF.c2: No price target or valuation endpoint. A forward price-to-sales multiple is the current multiple.
KRKNF.c4: Integration with more than 30 vehicle platforms is described. It is not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
KRKNF.c5: No named person's operating result is given with figures. The company missed last year's revenue estimate.
KRKNF.c6: The market cap is lower than before a deal that added about $300 million of revenue, and the guide was kept after a soft quarter. The article does not say what forces that gap to close.
KRKNF.c7: A stronger second half, with Covelya in the third and fourth quarters, is named and not given a report date.
flags: Q2 revenue grew only 4%, and the company missed last year's revenue estimate.
One contract can swing a quarter.
2027 growth includes a full year of Covelya that is not all organic.

LNC.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of LNC either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.
LNC.c1: The case is that the capital repair is done and the shares are still cheap. The author says future growth is likely to be slower.

LNC.c4: An insurance franchise is described. It is not argued as one of the five moat types with a mechanism, a trend, and a threat.
LNC.c5: The RBC ratio was rebuilt from below 400% to above 420%. No person is named with that result.
LNC.c6: The market is still pricing the 2022 capital scare. The correction is that the risk-based capital ratio is above 420%, operating earnings already annualize near $9 a share, and peers trade nearer 1x book and 6x to 7.5x earnings.
LNC.c7: The third quarter of 2026 is named as the next check, without a calendar date.
flags: The author says growth is likely to be slower as risk is transferred away.
Rates above 5% make the 4.45% yield less attractive.
The path from the capital repair to a $75 value can still take a long time.

URGN.c7: An NDA for UGN-103 is expected in the third quarter of 2026, with approval anticipated in 2027. That quarter is inside 24 months and is tied to the lead franchise.

XRX.long: I/we have a beneficial long position in the shares of XRX either through stock ownership, options, or other derivatives.

The author says good returns on the recycling plants still have to be shown.
Getting to $8 a share is a positive scenario, not the base forecast.
The dividend yield above 5.4% is part of the author's stated return and is not in the price math.

nLIGHT is described as better placed on high-energy lasers, and the large primes are investing in the same field.
Revenue is lumpy and the sales cycle is one to three years.

GLP-1 drugs could shrink the MASH market the model is built on.
